subject: MSA redlines: liability cap and SLA credits — interaction and carve-outs
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Wu <sara.wu@olivetech.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: MSA redlines: liability cap and SLA credits — interaction and carve-outs

Sara — attaching our current redlines (MSA_Redlines_2026-03-12.docx) and a short note on the key points OliveTech legal asked about. High level asks from OliveTech: increase the liability cap, remove credits as sole remedy, and broaden exclusions to exclude certain third-party claims.

Quick summary of our proposed positions (so legal has context):
- Liability cap: we proposed 3x the fees paid in the prior 12 months or $500,000 (whichever is greater).
- Exclusions: carve out claims for confidentiality breaches and IP infringement from the cap; do not exclude gross negligence or willful misconduct.
- SLA/service credits: OliveTech wants credits not to be the-only-available remedy; they want to reserve right to seek damages beyond credits. We want credits to be the sole and exclusive remedy for service availability failures so downtime claims can’t be converted into large damages.

Key question for legal: can we preserve a sole remedy for SLA credits while still allowing the liability cap to survive for other categories (e.g., IP/confidentiality)? Also, should our SLA credit payments count against the liability cap? If credits reduce the cap, they could undermine our protection for catastrophic claims.

Suggested redline approaches in the doc:
1) Add explicit carve-outs where liability cap does not apply (IP infringement, breach of confidentiality, personal data loss, and willful misconduct).
2) Keep SLA credits as sole and exclusive remedy for availability but specify a per-incident and aggregate cap on credits that is separate from the liability cap — or alternatively, expressly exclude credits from the calculation of damages subject to the general liability cap.
3) If we cannot get credits excluded from the calculation, add a higher overall cap for obligations arising from outages that exceed normal fees (i.e., a separate operational damages bucket).

Can you and Aditya review and tell me the language you'd like Legal to propose? I want to send a short note back to OliveTech legal by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Neha
Neha Kapoor

Subject: Re: MSA redlines: liability cap and SLA credits — interaction and carve-outs

Looping in a few commercial points from my side:
- We typically push for credits = sole remedy for availability because customers often try to convert uptime issues into consequential damages (lost profits).
- For enterprise deals we sometimes concede that credits are not the only remedy if the damages relate to confidentiality/IP — but we need those categories carved out from the normal liability cap.
- Practically: ask Legal to propose two clauses: (A) "Sole remedy for SLA" language that is tightly scoped to Availability SLA failures and excludes catastrophes (e.g., data breach, IP). (B) "Credits do not count towards the monetary liability cap" OR "Credits are excluded from the calculation of the cap."

If OliveTech insists credits are not the sole remedy, we should get: (i) a per-incident cap on credits (e.g., max credit = monthly subscription fee), (ii) an aggregate credit cap (e.g., 6 months of fees) and (iii) an explicit carve-out that keeps confidentiality/IP/willful misconduct outside any limitation.

Aditya

VP, Sales Operations

Subject: Re: MSA redlines: liability cap and SLA credits — interaction and carve-outs

Internal legal note for Neha before we go to OliveTech legal: our sort of "standard" MSA logic is:
- Baseline liability cap: greater of $500K or 3x fees in prior 12 months.
- Exclusions from cap: (i) breach of confidentiality (ii) IP infringement (iii) death/personal injury (if applicable) (iv) willful misconduct/gross negligence.
- SLA credits: we make them the exclusive remedy for uptime/availability. Credits should either be expressly excluded from the cap calculation or be subject to an independent credit cap (so they can’t be used to wipe out protection for other claims).

Also, practical negotiation tip: offer OliveTech a small increase to the cap (e.g., 4x fees instead of 3x) in exchange for maintaining the credits-as-sole-remedy position, and keep carve-outs for confidentiality/IP. This often gets us across the line in mid-market deals.

I can draft suggested legal language for the SLA paragraph and a short negotiating playbook you can send to their counsel. Want me to draft and send to Legal and cc you?

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Commercial Contracts
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: MSA redlines: liability cap and SLA credits — interaction and carve-outs

Neha — thanks for the summary and the redlines. OliveTech's legal team provided a counter: they want SLA credits to be available in addition to other remedies (i.e., not sole remedy), and they asked that credits be treated as recoverable damages that count toward the overall liability cap. Their reasoning is they want a single bucket for all remedies to ensure total recovery is predictable.

They are open to keeping carve-outs for IP and confidentiality, but they want to tighten the definition of "willful misconduct" so fewer claims fall outside the cap.

Can you send over Redwood's proposed alternative language for: (1) a standalone SLA credit regime that is explicitly outside the cap calculation, and (2) an option where credits are included but subject to a clearly defined aggregate cap (so we don't get unlimited exposure)? We'd like both options in writing so our GC can compare.

One administrative note: our procurement team needs to know whether any credit payments will be netted against future invoices or issued as refunds — please indicate preferred approach in your proposed language.

Best,
Sara
Sara Wu
Head of Procurement, OliveTech
sara.wu@olivetech.com

Thanks Sara — appreciate the clear counter. Attached are the two alternative snippets we propose (included in the redline doc):

Option A (preferred):
"SLA Credits as Sole and Exclusive Remedy for Availability Failures. If Redwood fails to meet the Availability SLA set forth in the Order Form, Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for such failure shall be the service credits expressly set forth in the Order Form. Service credits shall be paid or credited to Customer within thirty (30) days and shall not be treated as damages for the purposes of the Liability Cap. The liability cap set forth in Section X shall not apply to claims arising from breach of Customer Data confidentiality or Intellectual Property infringement. This section does not limit Customer's remedies for claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, which shall remain subject to applicable law."

Option B (alternative if OliveTech cannot accept sole remedy):
"SLA Credits as Priority Remedy with Aggregate Cap. In the event of Availability failures, Customer may elect to pursue service credits under the Order Form or pursue monetary damages. Service credits and any monetary damages recovered related solely to Availability failures shall be subject to an aggregate cap equal to the greater of $750,000 or twelve (12) months of fees paid by Customer. Service credits, if elected, shall be applied within thirty (30) days and shall be included in the calculation of the aggregate cap for Availability-related claims. Notwithstanding the foregoing, claims for breach of Customer Data confidentiality and Intellectual Property infringement shall remain outside any limitation of liability."

Operational note: we prefer to issue credits against future invoices (netting) for administrative simplicity, but we can pay refunds on request and pass that back to procurement to document.

If OliveTech prefers a revised definition of "willful misconduct," please have Legal propose specific wording and we'll review.

Neha
